import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick

# Load the dataset from the specified path
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots for a professional look
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots. This gives us more control over customization.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the bar plot. Seaborn's barplot automatically calculates the mean of the 'y' variable,
# which in this case (y='survived') is the survival rate.
sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='who',
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'],
    hue_order=['woman', 'man', 'child'],
    palette={'woman': '#4b0082', 'man': '#008080', 'child': '#ff8c00'},
    ax=ax,
    ci=None  # Disable confidence intervals for a cleaner look
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title('Titanic Survival Rates: Class and Demographics Mattered', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=15, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=15, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages for better readability
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mtick.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

# Add data labels on top of each bar for precise values
for p in ax.patches:
    # Do not annotate bars with zero height
    if p.get_height() > 0:
        ax.annotate(
            f'{p.get_height():.0%}',
            (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
            ha='center',
            va='center',
            xytext=(0, 12),
            textcoords='offset points',
            fontsize=12,
            color='black',
            weight='semibold'
        )

# Customize the legend
legend = ax.legend(title='Demographic', loc='upper right', fontsize=12)
plt.setp(legend.get_title(), fontsize='13')

# Remove unnecessary spines for a cleaner, more modern look
sns.despine(left=True)
ax.grid(axis='x') # Keep horizontal grid lines for y-axis reference

# Adjust layout to ensure everything fits without overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure as specified
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
